final_model_review.mathematical_explanation: The proof is correct. Injectivity gives ker(T) = {0}. By the rank-nullity theorem, dim V = dim ker(T) + dim im(T), so dim im(T) = dim V. Since im(T) is a subspace of the finite-dimensional codomain V with the same dimension as V, im(T) = V; hence T is surjective.

The proof correctly establishes the essential nonautomatic point: coset multiplication is well-defined. In node 3, the displayed factorization of (ab)^{-1}(a'b') is correct, normality places the conjugate b^{-1}(a^{-1}a')b in N, and subgroup closure places the product in N. Node 4 omits explicit checks of the remaining group axioms, but these are standard short inherited verifications: closure is built into the definition, associativity follows from associativity in G, N is the identity coset, and a^{-1}N is the inverse of aN. Under the stated ordinary-textbook rubric, those implicit inferences are sufficient.

The proof correctly verifies the two-sided ideal criterion. The kernel is nonempty because it contains 0_R, and closure under subtraction makes it an additive subgroup. For every r in R and x in ker(phi), multiplicativity gives phi(rx) = phi(r)phi(x) = 0 and phi(xr) = phi(x)phi(r) = 0, establishing closure under multiplication from both sides even when R is noncommutative.
